page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-64GB is a compute-oriented cloud instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 32 shared vCPUs running on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 64.0 GB of main memory, maintaining a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. This profile includes no bundled local disk storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent state and separate network configuration for public connectivity. The hardware also lacks discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate competitive throughput in multi-threaded environments. The instance scores 17101.0 in Geekbench multi-core testing, accompanied by a Geekbench single-core mark of 2082.0. Multithreaded decompression through bzip3 yields 227.04 GB/sec, while PassMark encryption achieves 37135.43, both placing in the top quartile. In contrast, stress-ng single-core compute performance registers at 787.38, falling in the bottom decile. Large language model execution is similarly constrained by the absence of dedicated matrix hardware, processing prompts on a 70B parameter model at 6.88 tokens per second.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory distribution, this server offers dense parallel capacity. The shared CPU allocation introduces trade-offs in workload predictability under peak host utilization compared to dedicated cores, but it delivers cost efficiency for burst-tolerant concurrent processing. Best-fit deployments include container orchestration nodes, multi-threaded continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data transformations, and decoupled microservices utilizing detached block storage.
